# Data the figures need from `analysis` (experiment-repo)

One tidy table per level, CSV or Parquet, one row per unit named below. Column names are
what the generators read; if analysis prefers other names, say so in the issue and I adapt.

## `cells.csv` — one row per (cell × estimator)
cell_id, graph (SBM/ER/BA/WS/Stanford3/ego-Facebook), n, mean_degree d, mechanism (a..f),
s (spillover share), p, sigma, design (bernoulli/cluster), cluster_resolution, cluster_modularity,
edge_noise_q, tier (G/A/O), estimator, n_draws, bias, sd, rmse (all divided by fixed tau=1),
rmse_mc_lo, rmse_mc_hi (MC 95% CI), bias_mc_lo/hi, sd_mc_lo/hi, sign_error_rate, coverage,
ci_width, L (leverage), S (spec-disagreement), corner_dist_treated, corner_dist_control,
dm_bias (measured in that cell).

## `ratios.csv` — regression/DM RMSE ratio per cell
cell_id, estimator, log_ratio, log_ratio_lo, log_ratio_hi (paired CI: ratio is of paired draws,
not a ratio of two marginal CIs), s_oracle, s_estimated.

## `diagnostic.csv` — Fig 7 / Table 2
cell_id, group_mech, group_family, pred_logrmse_combined, pred_logrmse_best_benchmark (both
held-out under leave-one-group-out), realised_logrmse; `diagnostic_groups.csv`: group, kind
(mechanism/family), r2_gain, lo, hi; `acceptance.csv`: criterion, value, threshold, ci_lo, ci_hi, met.

## `calibration.csv` — Table 1 / appendix sanity
mechanism, s, tau, tau_direct, dm_bias, snr, noise_var_share, null_check_error (sigma=0 correct spec).

## Provenance
Every file carries a sibling `<name>.meta.json`: git commit of the computing code, seed(s),
n_draws, date, and the script that wrote it. I print this in the appendix and check that every
plotted cell exists in the analysis plan.

## Agreed with analysis (experiment-repo#2)
Tier-G grid is full s{0,.25,.5,.75} x mechanisms (a)-(f) at every core (d,p); `ratios.csv`
interval is a paired two-level bootstrap; per-draw errors are saved. Coverage, sign-error and
ci_width per cell are needed for F9 and T3.

## Superseded by the analysis role's actual schema (make_cells.py, make_diag.py, make_calibration.py)
The generators read `cells.parquet`, `ratios.parquet`, `diagnostic*.csv`, `acceptance.csv`,
`calibration.csv` as written by experiment-repo; `figtab/common.py::load` maps their codes
(estimator `chin`->Chin, design `bern`->bernoulli, `d_target`->`mean_degree`, null column mechanism
"0") to display names. Ratios are natural-log RMSE ratios with a paired bootstrap over graph draws.

A push to your repository's `main`, or to `dev` of `paper-repo` (below), is a delivery; a local commit is not. # Reproduction notes

Everything in `results/` is computed by the code in `code/` from synthetic graphs, two public real graphs and the seeds below.
Nothing is copied from the literature. CPU only. The figure and table scripts are described in the last section.

## 1. Environment

Python 3.11.2, CPU only. Pinned versions in `code/requirements.lock`: numpy 2.4.6, scipy 1.17.1, pandas 3.0.6, pyarrow 26.0.0,
scikit-learn 1.9.1, networkx 3.6.1, matplotlib 3.11.2. Every script sets one thread per process (`OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`); runs are independent.

```
pip install -r code/requirements.lock
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD/code/src
```

## 2. Data

No experimental data is used: treatments are randomised by the code and outcomes are generated from the interference mechanisms.

Synthetic cells: 10 graph draws x 300 assignments = 3000 assignments per run, bootstrap (B = 100) on the first 30 assignments of each graph.

## 1. The story in one paragraph
Regression-adjustment estimators of the global average treatment effect (GATE) under network interference (Chin 2019; Han–Ugander 2023) fit outcome on functions of the assignment (own treatment, treated-neighbour fraction, …) and predict at all-treated and all-control. Published work shows they *can* work but gives no account of *how well, why, and when not*. We treat the estimator as **extrapolation from the observed exposure distribution to the two global corners** and ask what that predicts. The error splits into a **variance part** (OLS leverage of the corner contrast, scaling like d/(p(1−p)n)) and a **bias part** (curvature of the response × raw distance of the corner from the observed exposure support, roughly *not* growing with degree). The two parts have different drivers and, for the fraction feature, are predicted to move in opposite directions with degree (count, 2-hop and threshold mechanisms have their own predicted scalings), so "error grows with degree" is predicted to hold only where noise dominates. Abstract wording stays conditional until C2 is in. We test these scalings across interference mechanisms, graph families (synthetic and two real Facebook graphs), treatment probabilities and designs (Bernoulli, graph-cluster); map where regression beats and loses to difference-in-means (DM) and to exposure-mapping HT/Hájek; ask whether flexible/data-adaptive learners help; and test a data-computable two-part diagnostic against pre-registered trivial predictors. Not a new estimator: a verified, predictive account of when to trust an existing one. Positive, negative and mixed outcomes are all reported.

- *Regression GATE estimators*: Chin 2019 (estimator; Fig. 2 already shows the exposure-distribution mismatch qualitatively and draws the off-policy analogy), Han–Ugander 2023 (covariate generation/selection, block bootstrap). **We do not claim the extrapolation viewpoint as new**; we claim the quantified decomposition, its tests across mechanisms/graphs/designs, the regime map including where regression loses, and the diagnostic.
